cards.text: Asaph, the psalm's writer (Psalm 78:1), is still telling his people their history, so their children won't be stubborn like their fathers (Psalm 78:6-8). He's already sung about God splitting the sea and feeding them in the wilderness (Psalm 78:13, 24). Now he says, "How often they disobeyed Him in the wilderness and grieved Him in the desert!"

cards.question: True or false: Asaph says Israel tested God only once in the wilderness.

cards.text: Then Asaph says, "They did not remember His power…" I forget ONE timer and the whole Dorinverse smells like smoke, but they forgot the day God REDEEMED them!
That's when God performed His signs in Egypt and His wonders in the fields of Zoan, a region of Egypt (Psalm 78:12). First on the list, He turned their rivers to blood.

cards.question: True or false: With their rivers turned to blood, the Egyptians could still drink from their streams.

cards.text: Next come swarms of flies that devoured them, and frogs that devastated them. One frog hops out of my oven and I'm on the CEILING, gold base and all.

cards.question: God gave Egypt's crops to the grasshopper and the locust. Then the hail came. What did the hail strike?

cards.text: Then God unleashes His fury on Egypt, a band of destroying angels, and does not spare them from death. He strikes all the firstborn of Egypt.

cards.question: Why does Asaph list all these signs God performed in Egypt?

answers.text: To show the power Israel forgot
To show how proud Pharaoh was

cards.text: Then Asaph turns to God's own people. He led them out like sheep and guided them like a flock in the wilderness.

cards.question: True or false: Asaph says God led His people safely, so they did not fear.
God led His people safely. What does Asaph say happened to their enemies?

cards.text: Then He brought them to His holy land, to the mountain His right hand had acquired. I bet that felt like pulling into your driveway after the longest road trip of your LIFE.

cards.question: God drove out nations before Israel and gave the tribes their ___.

cards.text: You'd think that's the happy ending, but nope. They tested and disobeyed God Most High, for they did not keep His decrees.

cards.question: True or false: Asaph says Israel's tribes turned back and were faithless like their fathers.

cards.text: Asaph says they were twisted like a faulty bow. I had a warped cookie sheet once, and every single batch slid off it like it was trying to ESCAPE.

cards.question: Israel enraged God with their high places and provoked His jealousy with their ___.

cards.text: God hears it, friend, and He is furious. He rejected Israel completely and abandoned the tabernacle of Shiloh, the tent He had pitched among men.

cards.question: God delivered His strength to captivity and His splendor to the hand of the adversary. Then He surrendered His people to the sword. What reason does Asaph give?

answers.text: He was angry with His own people
He wanted to test their strength
They had asked Him for a king

cards.text: This part is heavy: fire consumed His young men, and their maidens were left without wedding songs. His priests fell by the sword, but their widows could not lament.
Then everything turns. The Lord awoke as from sleep, like a mighty warrior overcome by wine.

cards.question: Then the Lord beat back His foes. He put them to everlasting ___.
True or false: After God rejected the tent of Joseph and refused the tribe of Ephraim, He chose no other tribe.
God chose the tribe of Judah and Mount Zion, which He loved. Asaph says, "He built His sanctuary like the heights…" What else does he compare it to?

answers.text: The earth He has established forever
A tent pitched for a season
A river that never runs dry

cards.text: Then God chose David His servant and took him from the sheepfolds. David's whole résumé at this point? Sheep.

cards.question: David went from tending the ewes to what new job for God's people?

cards.text: So David shepherded them with integrity of heart and guided them with skillful hands. That's where Asaph lands this whole long song, friend.
